cells.tense: You are choosing one direction on purpose, and the practice is carrying it right now.
cells.act: hold your shape under the weight
cells.ask: Next session, keep the same weight, the same target, the same number of rounds, and stay a round longer than usual. Keep your form where it is while it presses.
cells.core:
You are choosing one direction on purpose here, and the hours are carrying it. At the bench, alone, your attention is on the work and you are not arguing with yourself about whether to be there. This is what it looks like going well: one thing, plainly named, kept to for a stretch, with nobody else needing to approve it.

Holding without forcing is the next rep, not a new plan. Keep the weight, the target and the rounds exactly where they are, and stay one longer than usual — no fresh numbers, no measurement against someplace you meant to be. Afterwards, note what the pace is teaching in the body rather than in the plan. What you have now is what you said you wanted it to become.

cells.tense: Where this practice will be is being forced hard before it has happened.
cells.act: look at the same thing longer, until it shows you more
cells.ask: Over these next sessions, stay with one piece beyond the usual stopping point and add no goals to it. Let what is on the bar today be what it is.
cells.core:
Every session is aimed at a version of you that does not exist yet — the one past the plateau, the one for whom the hard part is done — and the pull goes toward that instead of toward what happens tonight. The grip sits in a later hour, and what gets skipped is the hour actually at the bar.

Stay with one piece past the usual stopping point, and review nothing while you are there. Add no goals. The weight worth knowing is the weight on the bar today, held a little longer, unchanged. Let a thing show you what it already is before deciding what it should become. Form arrives through repetition, not through a sharper picture of the finished version.

cells.tense: What this practice used to be is the ground you have been set down on.
cells.act: do one thing today the way only you do it, and do not explain it
cells.ask: Do a small piece of the practice today the way you did when it was alive — one set, one page, one move that is yours — then set it down. No plan after, no starting over.
cells.core:
The practice you remember ended, and its measure is still the one you check the day against. Nothing has taken its slot, so anything new reads as smaller, and the hours go unused. That is what sits at the bench: not a missing plan, but a comparison running in the background while the work waits.

Nothing has to be rebuilt from there. Do one small piece today the way you did when it was alive — one set, one page, one move that is yours — and then set it down. No plan afterward, no starting over. What is already yours does not need a rebuild to be real. The hours exist; the doing is what has been missing.

cells.tense: The practice is being continued, and the one continuing it is not consulted.
cells.act: do the thing in your own way, without proving it
cells.ask: Before your next session, look at a piece of the routine you have been carrying by momentum and settle whether it stays or goes — as a decision, not a drift.
cells.core:
The short sits, the thin reps, the bare minimum that still counts as showing up — all of it is a direction, and it is running itself. Asked about it, you might say that is just how things are. From outside, the habit and the choice wear the same shape, and only one of them can be signed.

Before your next session, look at a piece of the routine you have been carrying by momentum and settle whether it stays or goes — as a decision rather than a drift. Either answer is fine. What matters is that the hour belongs to someone who chose it rather than to the slip of days. Nothing else about the week needs to change.
